overall_summary: The channel's growth is heavily driven by space and cosmic anomaly content, specifically extreme exoplanets with mind-bending physical properties. In contrast, general psychology, brain trivia, and repetitive memory facts consistently underperform, failing to capture the audience's curiosity.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,019 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) are the top-performing videos on the channel.
winning_patterns.action: Focus content production on extreme planetary environments, utilizing high-contrast visual imagery (e.g., burning ice, ruby rain, coal-dark) in titles and hooks.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (max 53 views across multiple uploads) and 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) consistently fail to gain traction.
weak_patterns.action: Pause the production of standard brain and psychology trivia, reallocating those resources to high-concept space and cosmic 'what-if' scenarios.

next_video.concept: An ocean planet with waves larger than mountains and a core of hot ice.
next_video.opening_direction: Imagine an ocean so deep that there is no ocean floor—just a core of burning ice.
next_video.twist_direction: At the bottom, the pressure is so intense it forces water molecules into a solid state called Ice VII, which remains solid even at temperatures hotter than the sun.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high performance of extreme planetary physics and cosmic anomalies, similar to the burning ice planet video which achieved 1,055 views.

experiment: Test a 'What-If' space survival scenario, such as 'What If You Fell Into a Planet of Liquid Metal?', combining the high-performing exoplanet theme with cinematic storytelling to see if it increases viewer retention and engagement.
